records.plant_name: Nelson energy center
records.researcher_notes: The PJM cycle queue export of October 21, 2026 lists request AH1-718, Invenergy Nelson Expansion LLC, filed April 7, 2025, facility output 391 MW, energy uprate 11 MW, capacity uprate 38 MW, Active in Phase 3, in-service May 29, 2028. A second request, C01-1171 from Invenergy Nelson LLC, filed April 24, 2026, asks for a 66 MW energy and 6 MW capacity uprate by April 28, 2028. An earlier 575 MW request, AB1-089, was withdrawn on June 9, 2025. Capacity stays 315 MW until an uprate is in service. The PJM Cycle Service Request Status page (https://www.pjm.com/planning/m/cycle-service-request-status) is a script-driven grid, so its spreadsheet export of October 21, 2026 is kept in the repository's work folder under pjm and is not cited as a link.

records.plant_name: Monarch Rock Air data center campus (Rockford)
records.monitor_reason: A gas generation plan for this data center is not confirmed by any source I could read, and no capacity, equipment or permit is public.
records.researcher_notes: Monarch Rock Air, a company tied to Monarch Energy, plans a data center campus on Friday Road in Rockford, Illinois. A Rock River Current article from June 2026, based on state incentive records, says the campus has associated power generation and is a 1,400 megawatt phased data center. That is the size of the data center, not of any power plant. The task list mentions 250 MW of gas engines planned for 2027 from Monarch's own website. I could not confirm that: the Monarch page is built with scripts and showed no text about Illinois or engines, and other articles describe ComEd grid supply. Still unknown: fuel, number of engines, generating capacity and air permit. Check for an Illinois air permit application. If added later, the captive fields are captive industry use power and captive industry type data center.

records.plant_name: Hut 8 Illinois Project 4 data center
records.monitor_reason: The source gives a data center size of 50 MW and names no gas generation.
records.researcher_notes: Hut 8 announced four data center sites in Louisiana, Texas and Illinois. A Data Center Dynamics article says the Illinois site, called Project 4, totals 50 MW. The source does not say where in Illinois, and does not say the site will make its own power from gas. The possible-updates sheet row mentions 1.5 GW across Texas and Illinois, but the Illinois share is only 50 MW. Still unknown: town, power source, any gas turbines or engines and their capacity. It stays on the list only to see whether on-site gas is announced. If added later, the captive fields are captive industry use power and captive industry type data center.

records.plant_name: Joliet Technology Center data center campus
records.monitor_reason: The campus is approved at 1.8 GW of data center capacity, but no gas power plant is named.
records.researcher_notes: The Joliet city council approved the PowerHouse Data Centers and Hillwood campus in March 2026. A Data Center Dynamics article says it will offer up to 1.8 GW at full buildout, built in four phases, each with its own six-acre substation. The article describes grid substations and names no on-site gas turbines or engines. Still unknown: whether any on-site gas generation will be built, and its capacity. Only a gas plant tied to this campus would be added. If added later, the captive fields are captive industry use power and captive industry type data center.

records.researcher_notes: The PJM cycle queue export of October 21, 2026 confirms the Infrasure listing: AH1-718 is Invenergy Nelson Expansion LLC, 391 MW facility output, an 11 MW energy and 38 MW capacity uprate, filed April 7, 2025, Active in Phase 3, in-service May 29, 2028. The 391 MW is the facility output after the uprate, not an addition. No air permit for an expansion appears on the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency notice site. This is not a data center item. records.plant_name: Will County Facility LLC gas request (PJM C01-1569)
records.monitor_reason: PJM's first-cycle queue list shows request C01-1569 for 346 MW of natural gas generation in Will County, Illinois, from Will County Facility, LLC. It was filed on April 25, 2026 with a requested in-service date of 2029. PJM's page for the request at https://www.pjm.com/m/ProjectTransition/SISReportDetails?queueNumber=C01-1569 confirms the queue number, the developer, the Braidwood 345 kV Switchyard connection point and the filing date. That page does not give the size, the fuel or the county. Those are only in the full queue list. To see them, open PJM's cycle request status page at https://www.pjm.com/planning/m/cycle-service-request-status, click XLS under full export, and find row C01-1569. No news story, filing or other page I could find names the request.

records.plant_name: Byron to Wayne Thermal #1 Project, Lee County
records.monitor_reason: PJM request AB1-089, a 575 MW one-by-one combined cycle plant by Invenergy in Lee County, was withdrawn on 2025-06-09 after an interconnection agreement was posted. It may be the same project as the Nelson energy center expansion GEM already tracks.

verifications.note: AB1-089 Byron to Wayne Thermal #1 Project found

records.researcher_notes: PJM's queue file lists a 575 MW combined cycle plant called Byron to Wayne Thermal #1 Project in Lee County, from Invenergy Nelson LLC. It was filed in 2015 and withdrawn in June 2025. PJM's impact study confirms the 550 MW capacity and the combined cycle design. The site is near Nelson, where GEM already has a plant. Ask whether GEM has this as a separate cancelled unit before adding one. If not, add it as a cancelled unit with cancellation year 2025.

records.plant_name: Garden Prairie Energy Facility, Boone County
records.monitor_reason: PJM requests U3-021 and AB2-096 describe a 450 MW gas combustion turbine plant in Boone County, withdrawn in May 2022. It was never built. It would only be added as a cancelled project if it was public.

verifications.note: names AB2-096, Garden Prairie, 350 MW and 3 x 157.6 MW turbines
U3-021 and AB2-096 Garden Prairie Energy Facility listed as withdrawn

records.researcher_notes: PJM's impact study for request AB2-096 describes three 157.6 MW combustion turbines at a Garden Prairie substation in Boone County, a 450 MW plant. The request was withdrawn in May 2022. I found no news or permit page showing it was ever a public project. Add as cancelled only if a public source turns up.

records.plant_name: MISO J1839, Decatur ADM North 138 kV, Macon County
records.monitor_reason: MISO request J1839 is a 325 MW simple cycle gas turbine in Macon County with a signed interconnection agreement and a 2027 in-service date. It may be part of the Broadwing energy center GEM already has, or a separate unit.

verifications.note: J1839, Decatur ADM North 138 kV, 325 found

records.researcher_notes: MISO's queue lists J1839 as a 325 MW simple cycle gas turbine at the Decatur ADM North 138 kV substation, with a finished study and an in-service date of January 2027. GEM already tracks the Broadwing energy center (452 MW, combined cycle) at the same industrial site. They could be one project or two. Ask whether J1839 is a separate unit. If it is, add it as a new unit, status pre-construction, start year 2027.

records.researcher_notes: MISO hides the state, county and fuel on its newest requests. About 30 Ameren requests of 80 MW or more are active and cannot be placed. Examples are J4241, J4264, J4343, J4260 and J4254. Check again when MISO fills in the fields.
